claims.text: A 50% room-temperature cold-rolling reduction constitutes severe plastic deformation for the proposed high-entropy alloy.
Cold rolling followed by aging at approximately 600°C for 2 hours will produce a hierarchical microstructure.
Aging at approximately 600°C for 2 hours will promote a uniform dispersion of nanoscale precipitates.
The resulting hierarchical microstructure will contain refined grains interspersed with uniformly dispersed nanoscale precipitates.
Severe plastic deformation will refine the alloy's grain structure.
The refined grain structure will enhance ductility.
The refined grain structure will enhance strain-hardening ability.
Controlled nanoscale precipitation will produce dispersion strengthening.
Controlled nanoscale precipitation will increase Young's modulus.
The hierarchical microstructure will mitigate crack propagation.
Mitigation of crack propagation will improve fracture resistance.
The treatment will simultaneously improve strength, ductility, Young's modulus, and fracture resistance relative to conventional processing.
The treated alloy will show an approximately 10–20% increase in yield strength relative to the baseline.
The treated alloy will show an approximately 10–20% increase in Young's modulus relative to the baseline.
Conventionally cast and homogenized high-entropy alloys with coarse grains and minimal precipitate control typically exhibit a strength–ductility trade-off.
Cold-rolling reductions below 20% may be insufficient to produce the proposed synergistic property improvements.
Aging above approximately 700°C may eliminate the benefits through excessive grain growth or overaging.
The magnitude of the property improvements will depend on the high-entropy-alloy composition.
